searches.outcome: OpenAlex HTTP 429; arXiv fallback timed out. No successful result and no conclusion about JWST observations.

limitations: The CLI resolves comet-1p to Halley, which also matches mathematics and Antarctic research. It fetches at most 50 candidates and keeps at most 20; open-access availability and relevance precede publication year in its ranking.

The date-sorted query still matches other Halley-type comets. The 2015 lightcurve and 2025 rendezvous papers below were found separately; neither appeared in the 45-record nucleus query. Absence from these results is not absence of research.
No MAST moving-target archive search was completed; actual JWST observations remain unverified.

inspections.result: Figure 8a is a newly published processing of Giotto imagery, visually inspected from the publisher PDF. The author warns that some smallest features may be artifacts. No input-frame list, numerical camera-to-shape controls or calibrated standalone raster is supplied with this figure. Unresolved as a surface replacement.

inspections.result: The 2017 paper cites this Venera image-processing study as its method. Its accessible abstract does not supply a reproducible Halley processing recipe. No conclusion about its unavailable full text.

inspections.result: Potential alternative rotation/shape-model route. Publisher PDF and ADS copy returned HTTP 403. Numerical solution and compatibility with the selected PDS shape remain unexamined.

Schleicher et al. (2015) reanalyse the 1985/86 narrowband photometry. This provides time-dependent lightcurve constraints; section 1 describes a future nucleus model. No camera-to-selected-shape solution was established in this inspection.

inspections.result: The review identifies a spherical-harmonic Halley shape derived from Giotto/Vega observations. The underlying numerical coefficients and original 2002 full text were not recovered. This remains a shape-model lead, not an excluded route.
Preparing for the 2061 return of Halley’s comet (2025) proposes a rendezvous. It identifies unresolved shape and rotation questions and supplies no newly observed nucleus surface dataset.
